active_projects.description: Research the shape of a semantic goal and its witnesses for the semantic proof mode, so that the findings can be used to revise the reply to pull request #10 (draft at specs/reviews/pr-reviews-2026-11-21/pr10-comment.md; not yet posted) and to judge the fix requested on pull request #11. RESEARCH ONLY: the deliverable is a report; do not edit the comment, the records, or any Lean source, and post nothing. START FROM what is already known and do not redo it: specs/reviews/pr-reviews-2026-11-21/pr10-review.md (the review of records/semantic-proof-mode.md: idiom, consistency with the sibling records, the four clients, the ceiling, the measurement plan, the open points), specs/978_review_pr11_pointed_semantic_lemmas/reports/01_review-pr11-pointed-semantic-lemmas.md, and records/milestones.md (C1-C4, D4, joins 6 and 7). The soundness adapter is decided (D4) and the adoption threshold is set as revisable; neither is in scope. SUBJECT: records/semantic-proof-mode.md on the branch of PR #10 (head bdaa3b6d0, read with gh pr diff 10) proposes a tool for proving a formula true or false at a named point of a named model from supplied witnesses, measured on refute_allFuture_stab and refute_stab_allFuture_past (FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/PlusNonValidities.lean) and refute_modal_future and refute_sentDet (FormalSystem/StarLanguage/StarNonValidities.lean). QUESTIONS, each answered with evidence from the tree. (1) THE GOAL SHAPE. What a truth-at-a-point goal should look like in a tactic proof: the per-language predicates (TruthAt, PlusTruthAt, StarTruthAt), the generic TruthEnv form of FormalSystem/Semantics/TruthClauses.lean, or the At abbreviation over Point introduced by PR #11 (head c6cd983b7, FormalSystem/Semantics/PointTransport.lean and TemporalRules.lean). PR #11's At cannot be rewritten through by any clause lemma (rw and simp only both fail; only show works), and the fix was left to the author as either an at_def simp lemma or At-level statements of the clause lemmas. Determine which fix gives the goal shape an evaluator would recurse on, whether the choice constrains the evaluator, and what the four clients' goals look like under each. (2) THE WITNESS INTERFACE. A clause-directed positional argument list or named witnesses: write out, for refute_allFuture_stab, refute_modal_future and refute_stab_allFuture_past (three clause layers), what the supplied evidence is at each clause and how each interface would read; say which is legible at three layers and what the trial the record proposes should be judged on. (3) EVALUATOR BESIDE THE LEMMAS OR ONE MODULE WITH THE MODE: the considerations on each side given what (1) and (2) find, and what records/milestones.md assumes. (4) WHAT THE #9 BRANCH ALREADY TRIED. The semantic tactic layer on the PR #9 branch (head b3d8f6463: Semantic.lean, SemanticCore.lean, the Semantic* files beside them, ProofModeExtensionsTest.lean): what goal shape and witness handling it used, what worked, what of it is reusable under a separate prefix and registry, and what depends on overloading the l* commands. (5) PRIOR ART, briefly and only where it changes a recommendation: how other proof assistants or proof modes present checking truth in a concrete model from supplied witnesses. OUTPUT: a report ending with a section 'Implications for the replies' in two short parts: for #10, point by point, what the reply should ask for, what it should state as decided, what it can drop, and any claim in the current draft found wrong or unsupported; for #11, which of the two At fixes to prefer and why, if the research gives a reason. Keep that section short enough to revise the comment from directly. Channel: review work on channel B supporting milestones C1 and C2

active_projects.description: State pointed soundness once over TruthEnv, with TM, TM+ and TM⋆ as instances, so that the semantic mode adapter needs no per-language wrapper module (milestone D4 of records/milestones.md, join 7; the adapter paragraph of records/proof-mode-architecture.md). PHASE 1: prove star_soundness_in, the context form of TM⋆ soundness (a StarDerivationTree fc Γ φ, a frame in fc, a model, history, time and register environment at which every member of Γ is true, give truth of φ there), beside star_soundness_validIn in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity/Star/StarSoundness.lean. TM has soundness_in (FormalSystem/Metalogic/Soundness.lean) and TM+ has plus_soundness_in (FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity/Plus/PlusSoundness.lean); TM⋆ has only the empty-context validity form. StarSoundness.lean mirrors PlusSoundness.lean arm for arm, so the plus proof is the model, but this has NOT been attempted: establish first how the register environment is quantified in the premises and whether the three empty-context rules go through unchanged. PHASE 2: one class, at layer 3 under FormalSystem/Metalogic/, tying a language derivation relation to its TruthEnv truth predicate, with the three theorems as instances, and one generic theorem giving truth at a point from a derivation, frame-class evidence and truth of the premises. KEEP THE CLASS MINIMAL: proof_mode_abstract_frontend_interface will later constrain the object-level interface, and this class should be something that interface can require, not a second packaging of the connectives. DO NOT restate any language soundness theorem under another name; FormalSystem/Metalogic/ProofModeSoundness.lean on branch feat/proof-mode-semantics is four such restatements and is the shape to avoid. Sound direction only: guard with assert_not_exists against the completeness theorems, and import nothing under FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/. Tests instantiate the generic theorem at all three languages. Open to either collaborator; the done-when in records/milestones.md is the standard.

active_projects.description: Introduce a connective signature layer under FormalSystem so that TM and TM+ share one primitive signature and one set of derived operators instead of PlusFormula being a verbatim copy of Formula. PRIMITIVES STAY MINIMAL. Formula (FormalSystem/Syntax/Formula.lean) has six constructors (atom, bot, imp, box, untl, snce) and PlusFormula (FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/Formula.lean) restates all six and adds stab for the stability operator; that minimality is correct for TM and TM+ and is to be preserved. Do NOT adopt cslib's non-minimal expansion to primitive diamond, allFuture and allPast (cslib Cslib/Logics/Modal/Basic.lean has primitive and, or, box, diamond; Cslib/Logics/Temporal/Syntax/Formula.lean has primitive allFuture and allPast; the rationale and the 11-primitive target for the Bimodal layer are in cslib specs/181_bimodal_primitive_dia_always_historically/reports/01_bimodal-primitive-expansion-research.md, and cslib task 181 is still NOT STARTED so its own tree is inconsistent with that target). Non-minimality exists there to let one syntax serve minimal and intuitionistic propositional bases, since each classical interdefinability fails in a weaker logic; TM and TM+ are classical, so adopting it here would buy nothing and would move most of the views tier out of views and into the derivation tier as theorems. THE DEFECT IS DUPLICATION, NOT THE PRIMITIVE CHOICE. Eighteen derived operators are defined verbatim in both syntax files: after, allFuture, allPast, always, and, diamond, kMinus, kPlus, neg, next, or, prev, reflectTime, someFuture, somePast, sometimes and top. This is the syntax-layer root of the tmX / plusX name-pair duplication, and it violates principle 5 of records/proof-mode-architecture.md (languages are instances of an interface, not copies of a file). MODEL TO FOLLOW. cslib Cslib/Foundations/Logic/Connectives.lean (224 lines) is a working instance of the wanted shape and is directly portable: one class per primitive operator (HasBot, HasImp, HasBox, HasUntil, HasSince, HasNext), then PropositionalConnectives extending HasBot and HasImp and supplying neg := phi -> bot and top := bot -> bot as DEFAULT FIELD VALUES so the derived Boolean operators are written once, then a hierarchy of ModalConnectives, FutureTemporalConnectives, TemporalConnectives, LTLConnectives and BimodalConnectives with a bridge instance from BimodalConnectives to ModalConnectives. Four cslib languages share that one definition of neg and top. Note one tension to resolve rather than copy: cslib's ModalConnectives is box-only and minimal while its concrete Modal.Proposition carries a primitive diamond, so interface and inductive disagree there. DELIVERABLE. A signature layer under FormalSystem carrying one class per primitive operator including a stability class for the TM+ operator, a propositional class supplying the derived Boolean operators once, and a bimodal class, with Formula and PlusFormula as instances and the eighteen doubled definitions written once. ALSO ASSESS reducibility: all 35 definitions in FormalSystem/Syntax/Formula.lean are opaque defs and cslib uses abbrev for its Boolean and dual definitions, which unfold definitionally; making the pure Boolean and dual definitions here reducible would let part of the views tier be definitional rather than a table of view rows with unfolding lemmas, which bears directly on the views tier design in records/proof-mode-architecture.md. SEQUENCING. This sits BELOW the proof mode and is a prerequisite for proof_mode_abstract_frontend_interface, whose object-level class is to package the connectives among its members and which should require this signature rather than re-package it; a dependency edge is filed to that effect. Keep the Atom type fixed as it is; cslib parameterizes Formula over the atom type but that is a separate and larger change and is out of scope here. investigate_stability_as_modal_family may change whether the stability operator gets its own class or shares the Modal one; read its report if it exists but do not wait for it. ADDITIONAL DELIVERABLES (done-when of milestone D1 in records/milestones.md). (a) StarFormula (FormalSystem/StarLanguage) is an instance beside Formula and PlusFormula; it carries its own copy of next among others. (b) The interval operators are defined once on the signature: inclusiveUntil, inclusiveSince, release, trigger, weakUntil and weakSince, agreeing in argument order with Formula.release, Formula.trigger, Formula.weakUntil and Formula.weakSince (see the Argument-order trap note on Formula.release), and the clause lemmas of FormalSystem/Semantics/TemporalIntervals.lean (inclusiveUntil_iff, release_iff, weakUntil_iff and their past duals; that module arrives with branch feat/pointed-semantic-lemmas) are restated about them instead of about inline derived formulas. (c) One next and prev encoding: TemporalRules.next and prev of FormalSystem/Semantics/TemporalRules.lean, Formula.next, PlusFormula.next, StarFormula.next and the copy in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Expressiveness/SeparationZ/Syntax.lean are one definition or are tied by rfl rows in Tests/BimodalTest/Semantics/ValidityLayerTest.lean. (d) FormalSystem/Tactic/FormulaSyntax.lean, which matches TM and TM+ operator names only, reads the signature so that operator recognition reaches L⋆; the semantic evaluator of records/semantic-proof-mode.md has L⋆ clients. FIRST QUESTION FOR RESEARCH, to settle before any design: ONE HOME FOR THE DERIVED OPERATORS. FormalSystem/Semantics/TruthClauses.lean already defines the derived operators once, generically over the clause classes (TruthEnv, BotClause, ImpClause, BoxClause, UntlClause, SnceClause, StabClause and their bundles): neg, top, and, or, diamond, someFuture, allFuture, kPlus, after, somePast, allPast, kMinus, always, among others, as abbrevs, and every language (L, L-plus, L-star, L-minus, Open, Hybrid, Quant) instantiates those classes. A syntactic signature layer that defines the same operators again would be a second generic copy beside the per-language ones, which is the duplication this task exists to remove. Decide, with the options and the evidence for each stated: (i) the signature is the syntactic half of the clause classes, the clause classes extend it, and the operators of TruthClauses.lean move down to it; (ii) the clause classes stay the one generic home and the per-language syntax files take their operators from them; (iii) two layers tied by rfl rows, and why that would not be a wrapper to rip out later. The answer fixes where the interval operators and the next and prev encoding of deliverables (b) and (c) live, what the temporal rules of the proof mode are stated about, and how deliverable (d) recognizes L-star operators. State the import and layering consequences (TruthClauses.lean is at the semantics layer; syntax sits below it) and the cost to the open contributions that build on the current definitions.

active_projects.description: MILESTONE M22 (records/proof-mode.md), LANE: metatheory. Fragment conservativity: prove that each fragment's logic is conserved by every larger one, so that filing a statement at its smallest fragment is a theorem and not a convention. State the argument ONCE in parametric form and instantiate it per edge. EDGES (records/theorem-library.md, Conservativity): L into L⁺ is proved at all four frame classes (`plusDerivable_ofFormula_iff`) and is only indexed here; Boolean into ModalBoolean and Boolean into TemporalBoolean, with completeness of the smaller from FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/Propositional/; ModalBoolean with `□` into TM, which needs completeness of S5 for the `□`-fragment, not stated in the tree; TemporalBoolean into TM at each frame class, which needs completeness of the temporal schemata alone at that class, not stated in the tree; ModalBoolean with `□` into ModalBoolean with both operators, from the others or directly by the collapse. A fragment logic here is the set of TM axioms and rules whose statements lie in the fragment; research must first state each fragment's proof system precisely, as a predicate on TM derivations or as a calculus of its own, and say which. Do NOT state any unproved edge with `sorry`. The edge from L⁻ into L is a different question, answered in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity/README.md, and is out of scope. active_projects.description: MILESTONE M16 (records/proof-mode.md), STREAM: views. ARCHITECTURE (records/proof-mode-architecture.md): tier Views; filed under every family; modules the views modules. A rule's statement names only the operators of the family or interaction it is filed under: pure family modules contain no implication, and an interaction with Boolean is its own module. Proof mode: views tier. Add the tactics that change only how a formula is written: folding and unfolding a defined operator (`¬`, `∧`, `∨`, `↔`, `◇`, `F`, `G`, `P`, `H`, `X`, `Y`, always, sometimes, the inclusive and weak Until and Since forms, and the TM⁺ counterparts) and replacing a formula by one that is equal as a Lean term. A view uses definitions and formula equalities ONLY: no axiom, no derivation rule, no object context, no frame class. It leaves the judgment unchanged up to definitional equality or a cast, and it can fail only because the formula has the wrong shape. Logical rewriting (replacing `A` by `B` because an implication or equivalence is derivable) is NOT a view and stays in the derivation tier. Deliverables: (1) the fold/unfold tactics, acting on the goal or on a named hypothesis, at the head or at a named position; (2) the expansion lemmas they rest on, each a `rfl` or a stated formula equality, filed with the syntax of the operator they expand; (3) the operator-matching helper the elaborators use (`operatorArgs?` and the occurrence views) expressed through the same table, so that what a tactic sees as an operator and what a view folds agree; (4) tests and a guide page stating the tier boundary. The plan settles the tactic names (one fold/unfold pair taking an operator name, or one tactic per view; open decision 1 of the architecture record) and where the tier lives: it must sit BELOW the derivation tactics and import none of them, so that a separate semantic mode can use it too. COORDINATION WITH OPEN CONTRIBUTIONS. Three stacked pull requests from a collaborator are open against this area: #7 (logical rewriting `lrewrite` / `lsimp`, the congruence kit), #8 (Until/Since introduction, folding and ZTime unfolding, `linduction`, whole-judgment time reflection, `keeping`, strict leads-to rules) and #9 (a semantic mode, asked to be re-proposed separately). If #7 or #8 has merged, extract the views already inside them (the equality handler of `lrewrite`, the view-preparation pass of `lsimp`, the derived views in Positions.lean, `ltemporal_dual view`, the inclusive Until and Since definitions) into this tier and leave the logical rewriting where it is; do not write a second copy. If they have not merged, build the tier on the merged code and note the extraction as owed. DONE WHEN: every defined operator in TM and TM⁺ has a fold and an unfold with a test in each direction; a `#print axioms` check on a views-only script shows no object-language axiom is involved; a negative test asserts the wrong-shape message; and the guide page exists. DEPENDENCIES. Hard: none. Sequencing: `proof_mode_split_shared_test_and_guide_files`, for the family layout. Consumers: `proof_mode_always_sometimes_scopes` (always and sometimes are defined operators), `proof_mode_abstract_frontend_interface` (the interface states rules about defined operators directly, which views make possible) and through it `proof_mode_leads_to_invariance_library` (present-inclusive leads-to is a defined form). The derivation proof mode lives in FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/ and FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode/; FormalSystem/Theorems/ must not import FormalSystem/Automation/. Every new `throwError` path gets a negative test asserting its message (`#guard_msgs`).

active_projects.description:
Repair FormalSystem/Tactic/Meta.lean's buildContextExpr, which throws on every call and hard-fails modal_search on any box-headed goal.

MEASURED BUG (confirmed live at FormalSystem/Tactic/Meta.lean:113): the line is `let mut result <- mkAppM ``List.nil #[formulaType]`, but List.nil's type argument is IMPLICIT, so mkAppM raises "too many explicit arguments provided to @List.nil" on every input, the empty list included. Both consumers -- FormalSystem/Automation/Tactics/Search.lean:475 (tryModalK) and :527 (tryTemporalK) -- call it OUTSIDE their `observing?` block, so the exception propagates rather than being caught as a failed search branch. Consequence: `example : |-[FrameClass.Base] box (p imp p) := by modal_search` fails with that AppBuilder error.

FIX: apply one of two repairs, both already compiled and verified working: (1) `mkAppOptM ``List.nil #[some formulaType]`, or (2) `Lean.mkApp (Lean.mkConst ``List.nil [Level.zero]) formulaType`. Prefer whichever better matches the surrounding code's conventions. Also assess whether the two Search.lean call sites belong INSIDE their `observing?` blocks -- a genuine elaboration failure there should be a failed search branch, not a hard tactic error.

TESTS: existing coverage only `#check`s buildContextExpr without invoking it (deliberately -- the repair was out of scope for the test-coverage work that found this), which is exactly why the bug survived. Add a regression test that actually INVOKES buildContextExpr, on the empty list and on a non-empty list, plus a modal_search acceptance test on a box-headed goal. Fold these into Tests/BimodalTest/Automation/LemmaDBTest.lean, which already holds the MetaM probes for Tactic/Meta.lean's helpers.

VERIFICATION: `lake build` and `lake test` green with zero warnings; the box-headed modal_search example compiles; no new axioms.

BACKLOG NOTE: the proposal audit flags open task 955 (proof_mode_close_leaves_with_automation) as a possible duplicate at semantic score 0.47 with no shared paths. It is not a duplicate: 955 names modal_search only to rule it out as a default closer, is scoped to FormalSystem/Automation/Tactics/, and would CONSUME this broken function as a bounded fallback rather than repair it. 955 therefore depends on this task.

ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS. Proof mode: leads-to and invariance library. `lprogress` (composition of G(A → F B) guarantees) and `linvariant` (integer-time invariance) are leads-to and invariance rules in the TLA / UNITY sense. Extend them to the standard rule set for safety and liveness: invariance, leads-to transitivity and disjunction, and well-founded progress, each as a pure rule with a tactic. Two definitional points must be settled in the plan before any rule is proved. (1) G and F are STRICT here, so the existing `G(A → F B)` is irreflexive and says nothing about the present: standard rules such as `A ⇒ B` gives `A leads-to B`, or leads-to reflexivity, fail for it. ROUTE R3 -- THE DETERMINIZATION-FREE PROGRESS-MEASURE DESIGN. PAPER RESEARCH ONLY, FILE SCOPE: none, no Lean. Filed on the exact terms the completeness-line reopen decision record sets for this route (specs/archive/926_lean_completeness_line_reopen_decision_record/reports/01_completeness-line-reopen-ruling.md, the Reopening Terms table's R3 row and its recommendation 3), modeled on 879's P9 and on 901's own paper-only posture.

THE QUESTION. Does a determinization-free progress-measure argument for T3 (L-plus ZTime completeness of TM-plus + LC_n + mirror) exist, and what would it need? Deliverable is a VERDICT plus grounds and, on a positive verdict, a DESIGN -- never a theorem and never a Lean declaration.

WHY THIS ROUTE AND NOT THE OTHERS. The determinization obstruction (O1) is `Muller.toRabin_exists`, a `proof_wanted` at Cslib/Computability/Automata/DA/Conversions.lean:112 in the local CSLib fork, whose named consumer is the ban/lull mechanism. R1 -- proving it -- is KEEP CLOSED in this repository, and specifically on the CSLib `require` clause rather than on Recommendation 8's engine-content clause, because a general automata lemma is not sections 7-15 content. "File no task against R1 in this repository" is that record's recommendation 1. A determinization-free progress measure needs no Rabin determinization at all, so it is the one reopened route that bears on the completeness theorem itself while standing clear of both standing rulings.

WHAT A POSITIVE RESULT DOES NOT BUY, STATED UP FRONT. A positive design result does NOT authorize a Lean filing of the design, and this must be written into the report's own framing rather than discovered at its end. The engine-content clause is aimed at the RESULT, not at the lemmas used to reach it: a different construction reaching the same completeness result still trips it. Any Lean filing of whatever this task designs requires a separate, explicit Recommendation 8 reversal by the user, win or lose on the paper design.

DO NOT RE-DERIVE OR RE-MEASURE. (1) The determinization costing is settled: the construction of record is the APPEARANCE-RECORD (LAR) route, Thomas 1997 section 6.1 Theorem 6.5 with Remark 6.6 -- not Safra's and not Piterman's -- on the ground that the lemma's input `a : Muller State Symbol` is ALREADY deterministic, so no determinization construction is removing nondeterminism; the archived Safra/Piterman attribution is a misattribution as to this lemma, accurate only about the composite NBA-to-DRA step. Costed at roughly 1,000 lines over 4-7 phases. If a figure is ever needed, re-cost against those rather than re-measuring from scratch. (2) The acceptance-condition split is settled: a deterministic Muller automaton suffices for the Auxiliary-Atoms rule, which carries no acceptance condition, and does NOT suffice for the ban/lull mechanism, whose banned list is indexed by the automaton's accepting pairs and does not present as a Muller family without a walk-dependent choice only an LAR can make. (3) The architecture of record for the two-sided engine, including the level split, the eliminated cross-certification clauses, the chronicle seed lemma and the four-link Step 3-prime, is already written as a paper proof and is read, not re-derived.

WHERE THE PROGRESS MEASURE WOULD HAVE TO BITE. The ban/lull mechanism is the sole named consumer of the pair-indexed acceptance condition, so it is the component a progress measure must replace. Address, at minimum: what well-founded quantity decreases along a chronicle in place of the banned list; whether it can be read from the hue/type data the alphabet already carries, or demands new syntax the Auxiliary-Atoms rule's freshness side condition would have to admit; whether it survives the two-sidedness, where forward badness is prefix-invariant and backward badness is not; and whether the clock rule's canonical cut still supplies the anchor the level split relies on.

PROHIBITIONS, RULING-LEVEL AND NOT PREFERENCES. (a) NO Lean file is written, edited or filed, under any outcome. Sections 7-15 of the Reynolds engine -- the two-sided chronicle, ban preservation, lulls and hue scheduling, universal non-acceptance, the two-sided truth lemma, the final-frame assembly -- stay barred from any Lean filing under every reopened route, this one included. (b) NO `require` of CSLib in either form; no lakefile.toml edit, no lake-manifest.json edit; the `require` question is not re-opened on this route's account. (c) NO task is filed against R1, and no attempt is made on `Muller.toRabin_exists`, in this repository. (d) NO edit, commit or push in the CSLib fork at /home/benjamin/Projects/cslib. (e) NO upstream PR. (f) Do NOT amend specs/ROADMAP.md's existing Recommendation 8 sentence: the reopen record's recommendation 5 rules explicitly that no amendment is needed, because that sentence's truth is unchanged -- the ruling settles only which parts of each route are reachable without reversing it. (g) The assessment of why the chronicle quotient's OWN Saturation is doubtful -- countably infinite slices, the quotient is not an oriented forest -- is CORRECT and LOAD-BEARING, the reason the universal-cover route exists at all; it is read as a premise, not revisited. (h) No completeness claim lands from this task.

CONFLICT AVOIDANCE, STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN NEGOTIATED. FILE SCOPE is none: this task writes its own specs/ artifacts and touches nothing under FormalSystem/, Tests/, docs/, typst/ or any shared library file, so it collides with no live task's territory by construction -- not with the ladder-realization line, not with the final-frame tasks carrying R2, not with the algebraic chain. It also files nothing, so it cannot contend for a task number or a ruling with any sibling.

CONTINGENCY. A negative verdict is a COMPLETE outcome, not a failure: if no determinization-free progress measure is available, or one is available only at a cost exceeding the LAR route's own, record that with its grounds and with what the obstruction actually is. Either verdict leaves the CSLib `require` decision and Recommendation 8 exactly where they stand; neither is reversed, weakened or re-opened by this task's result.

active_projects.description:
OPTIONAL, FILED NOT SCHEDULED -- AND LOAD-BEARING AS A CHECK. This task stays unscheduled: status HOLD (user ruling 2026-10-03; prior_status not_started), dependencies [], nothing depends on it. What has changed since it was filed is the claim that "none of the L-plus programme's recommendations rest on it." That is no longer accurate. Its 2EXPTIME lower bound -- ARGUED, not formalized -- is the sanity ceiling that three live records cite against any proposed decision procedure for L-plus. It is load-bearing as a check even while unproved.

ITS ROLE: THE SANITY CEILING. Three records USE this task's argued lower bound as the bound-sanity check -- nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is a credible decision procedure. All three were re-verified against the tree on 2026-10-07 (task 738), at their archive locations:

1. specs/archive/718_omega_sequence_decidability_full_lplus/reports/02_ranked-route-analysis.md (archived), the "Complexity sanity check" bullet at line 258: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness reduction (filed, argued in both directions) is the lower bound; determinization-based upper bounds are doubly exponential, which is consistent. Any proposal cheaper than 2EXPTIME is prima facie wrong. No bound committed."

2. Task 719's description (ray layer, seam gluing and stab fibre; completed and archived at specs/archive/719_ray_layer_seam_gluing_and_stab_fibre, record in specs/archive/state.json -- now provenance rather than a live document), Deliverable 5: "DO NOT LAND A COMPLEXITY CLAIM; the CTL-star 2EXPTIME lower bound is the sanity check on any proposed bound."

3. specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/reports/01_decidability-programme-review.md (archived) section 3.1 (L-plus routes forward), line 147 -- its Section C ruling on this task is at line 183: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness argument (task 713, ARGUED) is the lower bound on any proposed procedure; nothing cheaper is credible; no bound is committed here."

ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED -- AND EVERY CITING RECORD MUST SAY SO. The bound is an argument in prose, not a machine-checked theorem. No Lean declaration establishes it; there is no CTL-star syntax or semantics in the tree to state it against. Every record that cites it must describe it that way, with the ARGUED qualifier attached, exactly as the three records above do. A citation that presents the bound as established, or that drops the qualifier, is a defect in that record.

NO UPPER-BOUND CLAIM MAY LAND FROM THIS TASK. The programme commits to no complexity bound. This task's content is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: it rules proposals out, it never certifies that any procedure achieves a cost. Deriving or landing an upper-bound claim from it -- in this task's artifacts, in a citing record, or in the write-up -- is a defect, not a result. The asymmetry is the point: a lower bound says "nothing cheaper is credible", it does not say "this much suffices."

GOAL. Raise the 2EXPTIME-hardness of L-plus Z-time validity from ARGUED to MACHINE-CHECKED. The argument is given in both directions in specs/archive/706_lplus_finite_model_property_and_completeness/reports/01_lplus-finite-model-property-research.md section Q4 ("The true order of the state bound"), completing what task 703's round-2 report argued in one direction only -- now archived at specs/archive/703_lplus_compression_and_completeness/reports/02_semantics-first-compression-research.md section 1.6 ("The complexity picture").

THE REDUCTION. Translate CTL-star by A |-> stab and X |-> bottom U ., with non-strict U rendered as e or (g and (g U e)). FORWARD: a rooted total Kripke structure becomes bi-serial by adding one fresh state with a self-loop and an edge to the root, which leaves forward paths from the original states unchanged; stab at (sigma, t) with sigma t = w ranges over histories through w, whose futures are exactly the forward paths from w, and the translation is pure-future so its truth depends only on the future (truth_congr_agreeFrom). BACKWARD: from a Z-model of the translation at (sigma, t), the Kripke structure of the state graph forward-reachable from sigma t satisfies the CTL-star formula at sigma t, by the same two facts read backwards. CTL-star satisfiability is over arbitrary, possibly infinite structures, so no finiteness is needed anywhere.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY. Formalization would turn the ceiling from an argued check into a theorem-backed one: the sharpest available limit on how good ANY certificate class can be. As task 706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6 record the consequence, with the reduction a theorem no complete certificate class with singly exponential, polynomially checkable certificates could exist for full L-plus without a complexity-theoretic surprise.

CANONICAL WORDING OF THE CONSEQUENCE (quote this, verbatim, in any record that repeats it). L-plus Z-time validity -- equivalently, by negation, L-plus Z-time satisfiability -- is 2EXPTIME-hard by the CTL-star reduction. ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED: no Lean declaration establishes it. CONSEQUENCE, stated for NON-VALIDITY: if every non-valid formula had a certificate of size singly exponential in the closure size, checkable in time polynomial in the certificate's size, then non-validity (satisfiability of the negation) would be in NEXPTIME and, equivalently, validity would be in co-NEXPTIME; hence 2EXPTIME would be contained in NEXPTIME, equivalently in co-NEXPTIME, since 2EXPTIME is closed under complement. That containment is not refuted but is widely disbelieved. The two class names are the same statement read from opposite sides of the complement: a record may name either, but must say which problem it is placing (NON-VALIDITY with NEXPTIME; VALIDITY with co-NEXPTIME). This is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is credible. It says nothing about any cost sufficing for L-plus and must never be restated as an upper bound. Sources: 706 Q4 (validity / co-NEXPTIME reading) and 703 round-2 section 1.6 (satisfiability / NEXPTIME reading), reconciled 2026-10-07 (task 738): the apparent divergence was one of presentation, not content.

WHAT IT COSTS. A CTL-star syntax and semantics must be added to the tree, which is substantial standalone work the programme otherwise has no need for. Task 706 rates the risk that the reduction has a gap as LOW (its R4) and records it as affecting the complexity picture only.

KEEP-OR-ABANDON IS A PHASE 0 USER RULING, NOT MADE HERE. This revision records the task's role; it does not decide the task's fate and does not schedule it. The decidability-programme review's Section C (specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/followup-scope-spec.md, Section C at line 220) restates the choice as the user's: keep this as a write-up note, or abandon it. RECOMMENDATION ONLY, not a decision: keep it as a write-up note, because it is load-bearing as a check even while unproved -- abandoning the record would leave the three citing documents pointing at nothing. If the ruling is to abandon, the three citing records need their sanity-check bullets re-sourced to the argument's actual homes (706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6) rather than to this task.

active_projects.description:
Acquire and ingest the Cmiel-Kuhlmann-Kuhlmann ball-space paper into the literature corpus, which currently has no copy of it.

Measured gap (verify rather than trust): the manuscript's def:frame carries a footnote citing \cite{Cmiel2021} for the claim that the nonempty fibers and segments form a BALL SPACE, and that Saturation is the downward-directed-intersection condition S_1^d of that hierarchy -- the nest condition S_1 with a directed system of balls in place of a nest. That citation has no local backing document: no entry matching Kuhlmann, ball space, spherically complete or ultrametric appears in ~/Projects/Literature/index.json or in specs/literature-index.json, and a filename search across ~/Projects/Literature/ returns nothing.

Why this matters rather than being bookkeeping. Research on the S1-versus-directedness question had to proceed without the primary source and was able to settle only part of it: S_1 provably suffices for the step lemma over every history with a countable domain (covering Z-time and Q-time), while directedness can only be forced over a non-archimedean duration type with an omega_1-coinitial positive cone. The converse direction S_1 -> S_1^d remains open, and the manuscript has already withdrawn its earlier "strictly stronger" wording in favour of "at least as strong as", so the strictness question is live rather than settled. Both the open direction and the ball-space framing route through the cited hierarchy, and neither can be grounded against the source while the source is absent. Note also that Mathlib has no spherical-completeness API at all, so there is no secondary formal reference to fall back on.

Scope: locate the paper (Cmiel, Kuhlmann and Kuhlmann, ball spaces; the manuscript's own bibliography entry is the starting point for exact title and venue), then run /literature to convert and index it so it is discoverable by future --lit dispatches. Record in the sub-index what the hierarchy's S_1 and S_1^d conditions are as the source states them, so later work can check the project's usage against the source's own definitions rather than against paraphrase.

Out of scope: any Lean change, and any edit to the manuscript.

The MCS-to-ultrafilter bijection is live at Algebraic/UltrafilterMCS.lean:782 (ultrafilter_correspondence), though stated existentially rather than as a named Equiv -- converting it to an Equiv may be worth doing here. READ THE PAGE IMAGES DIRECTLY (the Read tool's pages parameter); do NOT rely on a pdftotext-derived conversion for any axiom statement or equation. Blackburn/de Rijke/Venema 2002 Chapter 5 (corpus entry blackburn_2002) is the primary reference and is born-digital.

MATHLIB HOOK: Order/Atoms.lean:710 (toSetOfIsAtom : alpha <-> Set {a // IsAtom a} for CompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra) is the atom-structure half of Stone/Jonsson-Tarski for the complete atomic case and is the single most relevant Mathlib lemma here; supporting lemma eq_setOf_le_sSup_and_isAtom at :695. OPEN RESEARCH QUESTION, not an implementation task. Is the logic of C3 -- the domain-restricted consequence relation -- equal to Burgess-Xu without the unboundedness assumption, plus S5?

and NO Lean declaration states it -- confirmed by grep over `FormalSystem/` at filing time. Re-confirm that absence before writing anything, and if a declaration has since appeared, say so and stop: the premise of this task would then be stale.

What is NOT acceptable is a plan that assumes the dichotomy and builds the certificate class on top of it -- that is the shape this record exists to prevent.

IMPLEMENTATION TASK, small and self-contained: state and prove truth invariance for the open-future and open-past modals along a history morphism that lifts ray agreement, and derive such a lifting at ZTime from TwoWayBounded. This is the one formalization item recommended by the MSO-route research; it is independent of every unverified step in that route.

WHY THIS EXISTS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. The MSO route argues on paper that ZTime validity of the open language is decidable, and the open modals were confirmed to ride step 4's encoding -- see specs/866_mso_route_open_modals_ztime_decidability/reports/01_mso-route-open-modals.md, recommendation R1. That route is NOT being formalized and is not to be: Mathlib has no MSO syntax, no omega-automata, no determinization, and no Rabin tree theorem, so step 5 would mean a multi-year project of a different kind. This task lands only the semantic invariance lemma the route's cover step needs, which is useful on its own terms wherever open-modal truth must be transported along a morphism. Claim no decidability result and no completeness result here.

WHAT TO STATE. Three pieces, in this order:

(1) A ray-agreement lifting hypothesis beside HistMap.lift in FormalSystem/Semantics/HistoryMorphism.lean, as a standalone hypothesis or a new field: a history of the image frame agreeing with the image of tau' up to x lifts to a history of the source agreeing with tau' up to x. Then its time-reflected mirror for the open-past modal. Note that HistoryMorphism.lean's own docstring already records that HistMap.lift is derivable from TwoWayBounded.step rather than primitive, and that step is strictly weaker than lift -- read that discussion before choosing between a field and a hypothesis, and record the choice.

(2) The ZTime derivation of both from TwoWayBounded.step/forth via the existing forward/backward sequence machinery in the same module. The research notes the lifted witness reuses the given history's past verbatim and needs only forward lifting from the basepoint at x, which is strictly weaker than the two-sided HistMap.lift that plus_invariance's stab case already uses -- so this should be easier than the landed two-sided case, not harder.

(3) An open_invariance theorem over OpenFormula, reusing plus_invariance's seven cases. OpenLanguage sits above Semantics (OpenTruth.lean imports Semantics.Truth; nothing under Semantics/ imports OpenLanguage), so a new FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/OpenInvariance.lean can import HistoryMorphism -- confirm the aggregator wiring in FormalSystem/OpenLanguage.lean, and confirm the layering still holds before committing to the module site.

SIZE: estimated 150-350 lines, one implementation phase. IMPLEMENTATION TASK, small and fully templated: build `FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/Subformulas.lean`, the L^▷ counterpart of `FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/Subformulas.lean`. This is pure syntax, gated on nothing, and it is the one piece of L^▷ infrastructure that any native decision procedure over `OpenFormula` needs before it can be stated at all.

THE GAP, VERIFIED AT FILING. `FormalSystem/OpenLanguage/` holds nine files and no `Subformulas.lean`. A tree-wide grep for `openSubformulas`, `subformulasOpen`, `openSubformulaClosure` and `openComplexity` returns nothing, and no task in `specs/state.json` names any of them in a description or a `file_scope`. By contrast `PlusLanguage/Subformulas.lean` is 373 lines carrying `subformulas`, the per-constructor membership lemmas, `subformulas_trans`, `plusSubformulaClosure` as a `Finset`, `self_mem_plusSubformulaClosure`, the `decidableMemPlusSubformulaClosure` instance and the `plusClosure_*` closure lemmas one per constructor. L^▷ has none of it.

WHAT TO BUILD, mirroring that file constructor for constructor. `subformulas : OpenFormula -> List OpenFormula` over all nine constructors; the membership lemmas (`self_mem_subformulas`, `imp_left`/`imp_right`, `box_inner`, `untl_left`/`untl_right`, `snce_left`/`snce_right`, `stab_inner`, and the two new arms `ofut_inner_mem_subformulas` and `opast_inner_mem_subformulas`); transitivity; `openSubformulaClosure` as a `Finset OpenFormula` with its self-membership, its decidable-membership instance and one `openClosure_*` lemma per constructor. `OpenFormula` must have `DecidableEq` for the `Finset` layer -- check whether `Formula.lean` already derives it and derive it there if not, in the same phase.

THE AGREEMENT LEMMA THAT MAKES THIS A TRANSFER AND NOT A DUPLICATE. State `subformulas_ofPlus`: the subformulas of `ofPlus phi` are the `ofPlus`-images of the subformulas of `phi`, and the closure analogue. This is what lets a result proved by induction on L-plus subformula closure be re-read at L^▷ instead of re-proved, and it is the reason this file belongs to the transfer programme rather than being incidental library padding. This task belongs to the L^▷ exploration stage of specs/ROADMAP.md, off both critical paths: do not dispatch it ahead of, or batch it with, L-plus critical-path work. Its content below stands except where this paragraph says otherwise. SCOPE REVISED: DECISION RECORD ONLY. No removal is to be attempted, and no constructor of `OpenFormula` is to be deleted or re-expressed as notation: the stability modal stays primitive in both L-plus and L^▷. The deliverable is the Phase 1 gate alone, as a report: (1) whether any live consumer evaluates the stability modal off the regular class, where the backward half of the definability biconditional fails; (2) what losing state-locality would cost the decidability front and the atomization route; (3) a verdict on whether removal would be sound relative to this tree, recorded for a future ruling and not acted on. Every sentence below that names removal as a deliverable is superseded by this paragraph. Dependencies are reduced to the L^▷ proof-system task alone.

IMPLEMENTATION TASK WITH A DECISION GATE IN PHASE 1, and the gate is the point: remove the stability modal from `OpenFormula`'s primitive constructors, replacing it with notation for the open-past-of-open-future composite, OR record with compiled evidence why it cannot be removed. Entering this task committed to removal is the way to get it wrong; the removal is desired and must be attempted, but two specific obstructions are on record and the task is accountable to them.

THE REQUEST. The stability modal is definable in L^▷ -- the biconditional is landed, in both associations -- so carrying it as a tenth primitive constructor is redundant, and the maintainer's standing preference is that it go. This task owns that removal.

THE TWO OBSTRUCTIONS, BOTH ON RECORD AND NEITHER A GUESS. Read both before planning.
(1) THE BICONDITIONAL IS CLASS-RESTRICTED. The forward half holds on every regular task frame; the backward half needs `[F.IsRegular]`. So a syntactic abbreviation does not preserve the stability modal's truth conditions off the regular class -- it changes the language's meaning on exactly the frames where the two differ. Establish FIRST, as Phase 1's deliverable, whether any live consumer evaluates the stability modal off the regular class. If none does, removal is sound relative to this tree and the restriction is a documented precondition rather than a blocker. If one does, removal is refused on this ground and the task's outcome is that finding.
(2) STATE-LOCALITY IS LOST. The decidability front's one working anchor for the stability modal is that it is state-local -- one bit per cell, `stab_mem_tpOf_iff_cell` resting on `stab_state_only`. The open-future and open-past modals are not state-local; they quantify over agreement classes through the time of evaluation. Routing the stability modal through them discards that anchor. Phase 1 must measure what actually depends on it: enumerate the consumers of `stab_state_only`, `stab_mem_tpOf_iff_cell` and the cell-level stability reasoning, and say for each whether it is reachable from `OpenFormula` at all or lives purely on the other language's side of the embedding. The two languages are separate inductives, so a consumer that only ever sees the other language's stability constructor is NOT affected by removing this one -- establishing that is the cheapest possible route to a clean removal, and it may well be the actual situation. Do not assume it; measure it.

WHAT REMOVAL MEANS IF PHASE 1 CLEARS IT. Delete the stability constructor from `OpenFormula`; introduce the stability modal as notation or an abbreviation over the open-past and open-future composite; re-derive every landed stability result at `OpenFormula` from the composite form, including the pointwise S5 laws, the strength ordering, the reversal transport (the reflection operation fixes the stability modal and exchanges the two open modals, so the reflection arms change shape and must be re-proved rather than re-cited), and the stability arms of the truth recursion, the axiom type, the derivation tree and the soundness recursion. Both conservativity directions over the other language must be re-stated, since the embedding's stability clause is exactly what changes. The regularity precondition goes in the docstring of every result that now needs it, and in the theorem-index row's frame-class column.

ORDERING, AND IT IS A HARD GATE. This task must run AFTER the L^▷ proof system, the L^▷ substitution closure and the L^▷ incompleteness transfer have landed, and BEFORE the display-name rename. Rationale: each of those three lands new declarations that pattern-match on `OpenFormula`'s constructors, so removing a constructor first would force them to be written twice; and the rename should operate on a language whose constructor set is final. Declare all three as dependencies.

EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE. Do not touch the other language's own stability constructor, its axiom type or its derivation tree -- the standing ruling against mutating those inductives is unaffected by this task and the landed incompleteness and independence results depend on them unchanged. No completeness claim. No decidability claim. Do not weaken a landed result to a regular-class-only form in order to make removal go through without saying so: any result whose frame class narrows is a recorded consequence of this task, listed in the summary, not a silent edit.

THE HONEST OUTCOMES, and all three are complete. (a) Removal lands, with the regularity precondition documented. (b) Removal is refused on obstruction (1) or (2), with the blocking consumer named and compiled evidence recorded under the evidence-probe convention. (c) Removal lands at the regular class only, with the off-regular behaviour change stated explicitly in the module docstring and the theorem-index rows. A refusal with a named cause is a complete outcome and must not be reported as a failure.

LAYERING AND GATES. Add any new file's row to the layer table in `scripts/measure-refactor-partitions.py` in the same phase as the file or the cycle checker FAILS naming it. Close three small gitignore and loose-file hygiene gaps at the repository root.

Source of record: specs/reviews/review-2026-11-19.md (one Medium, two Low severity findings).

(A) MEDIUM -- retired latex/ build artifacts are untracked but unignored. The latex/ edition was deliberately retired and its .tex sources removed from git, and .gitignore gained a `latex/**/*.log` rule at the same time. The remaining build byproducts in latex/build/ and latex/subfiles/ (.pdf, .aux, .fls, .fdb_latexmk, .out, .toc, .xdv) are untracked yet matched by no .gitignore pattern, so they sit as unignored cruft and any future `git add` touching that path risks reintroducing retired build output into history.
    Fix: extend .gitignore with a single `latex/build/` rule (preferred over enumerating extensions), matching the intent of the existing `latex/**/*.log` line. Verify with `git status --porcelain --ignored` that the artifacts move from untracked to ignored, and confirm no currently-TRACKED file becomes ignored as a side effect.

(B) LOW -- `.pid` at the repo root is a stray runtime PID file, untracked but absent from .gitignore, unlike the sibling runtime paths .agent-logs/ and .playwright-mcp/ which are both correctly ignored.
    Fix: add `/.pid` to .gitignore (anchored, so it cannot match a nested path).

(C) LOW -- Challenge.lean at the repo root is a loose .lean scratch file containing a sorry-bearing theorem. It is not a Lake root (absent from lakefile.toml), is not built, and is not listed in ORGANISATION.md's "Everything else" table alongside the other top-level paths, so a reader cannot tell why it exists or whether it is safe to ignore.
    Fix: EITHER add one line to ORGANISATION.md's "Everything else" table explaining its purpose, OR relocate it into Boneyard/ following that directory's existing archival conventions (which are ADR-backed and gate-enforced -- read its README before moving anything there). Decide from the file's git history which is appropriate; do not delete it.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: Boneyard/ itself (verified deliberate, ADR-backed and gate-enforced -- not cruft); the already-gitignored other/, research/, training/ and data/ directories; and any change to lakefile.toml.

VERIFICATION: `bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh` and `bash scripts/readme-lint.sh` both no worse than before the change; `git status --porcelain` clean of the newly-ignored paths; no tracked file newly ignored.

proposal.title: Close gitignore and loose-file hygiene gaps at repo root

artifacts.summary: Research on the three gitignore/loose-file hygiene gaps: (A) the latex/build/ cruft is already fully covered by an existing generic build/ rule (review premise refuted by git check-ignore evidence, but adding an explicit rule is still worth doing for clarity); (B) /.pid is a confirmed, uncomplicated gap; (C) Challenge.lean is not a stray scratch file but the committed trust-boundary artifact of lean-challenge-snapshot.sh (the Comparator statement-pinning mechanism) -- it must be documented in ORGANISATION.md, not relocated to Boneyard/, which would break the mechanism.
Two-phase plan: .gitignore rules (latex/build/, anchored /.pid), then ORGANISATION.md row for Challenge.lean.
Two-phase implementation summary covering both .gitignore rules and the ORGANISATION.md Challenge.lean row.

active_projects.completion_summary: Added latex/build/ and anchored /.pid rules to .gitignore, and one Challenge.lean row to ORGANISATION.md's Everything else table documenting its Comparator-snapshot provenance. Both named gate scripts (check-module-invariants.sh, readme-lint.sh) confirmed no-worse-than-baseline; no tracked file became newly ignored; Challenge.lean itself untouched.
